title: Laborers in the Vineyard and True Greatness

questions.question: In the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard, what wage did the master of the house agree upon with the first workers early in the morning?
options: A portion of the grape harvest
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:2 (ESV): "After agreeing with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard."

questions.question: What time was the final group of laborers hired by the master, just before the day ended?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:6 (ESV): "And about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing. And he said to them, 'Why do you stand here idle all day?'"

questions.question: When evening came, the master ordered the foreman to pay the laborers. When the eleventh-hour workers were paid, how much did they receive?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:9 (ESV): "And when those hired about the eleventh hour came, each of them received a denarius."

questions.question: Why did the first group of laborers grumble against the master of the house?
options: Because the master made the eleventh-hour workers equal to them, though the first group bore the burden of the day and the scorching heat
Because they wanted their wage in gold
Because they were given less than a denarius
Because they wanted to own part of the vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Because the master made the eleventh-hour workers equal to them, though the first group bore the burden of the day and the scorching heat
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:11-12 (ESV): "And on receiving it they grumbled at the master of the house, saying, 'These last worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.'"

questions.question: What did the master tell the grumbling worker?
options: "Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?"
"You have been lazy so I deduct your wage."
"A denarius is all that your labor was worth."
questions.correctAnswer: "Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?"
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:13 (ESV): "But he replied to one of them, 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?'"

questions.question: How did the master justify giving the late workers the same wage?
options: "Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or do you begrudge my generosity?"
"They were starving and needed the money more."
"It is a rule given by the scribes."
"Because they worked harder than you in their single hour."
questions.correctAnswer: "Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or do you begrudge my generosity?"
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:15 (ESV): "Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or do you begrudge my generosity?"

questions.question: As Jesus went up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve aside and foretold His death again. He said He will be delivered to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and ________.
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:19 (ESV): "...and deliver him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified, and he will be raised on the third day."

questions.question: Who came to Jesus with her sons, kneeling down and asking a favor of Him?
options: The mother of the sons of Zebedee (James and John)
questions.correctAnswer: The mother of the sons of Zebedee (James and John)
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:20 (ESV): "Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came up to him with her sons, and kneeling before him she asked him for something."

questions.question: What did the mother ask of Jesus?
options: "Say that these two sons of mine are to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom."
"Give them ten cities to rule over."
questions.correctAnswer: "Say that these two sons of mine are to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom."
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:21 (ESV): "She said to him, 'Say that these two sons of mine are to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.'"

questions.question: Jesus told the two brothers, "You do not know what you are asking," and then asked if they were able to do what?
options: "Are you able to drink the cup that I am to drink?"
"Are you able to walk on water as Peter did?"
"Are you able to carry the cross alone?"
"Are you able to preach to the Pharisees?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Are you able to drink the cup that I am to drink?"
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:22 (ESV): "Jesus answered, 'You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am to drink?' They said to him, 'We are able.'"

questions.question: To whom does Jesus say it belongs to grant seats at His right and left hand?
options: "To those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
questions.correctAnswer: "To those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:23 (ESV): "...but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."

questions.question: How did the other ten disciples react when they heard about James and John's request?
options: They were indignant at the two brothers
They praised them for their ambition
questions.correctAnswer: They were indignant at the two brothers
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:24 (ESV): "And when the ten heard it, they were indignant at the two brothers."

questions.question: Jesus said the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, but whoever would be great among you must be your what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:26 (ESV): "It shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant,"

questions.question: Jesus concluded this teaching by saying, "even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a..." what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:28 (ESV): "even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."

questions.question: As they went out of Jericho, two blind men sitting by the road cried out to Jesus. What did they ask Him to do?
options: "Lord, tell us the way to Jerusalem."
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:33 (ESV): "They said to him, 'Lord, let our eyes be opened.'"

key_verse_text: "even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
